How do you care for a snake plant in the UAE?

Snake plant care in the UAE is simple: give the plant bright indirect light, water only when the soil is dry to the bottom of the pot, and use a pot with a drainage hole. Under AC the soil dries slowly, so test it before every watering. Overwatering, which leads to root rot, is the main reason a snake plant (Dracaena trifasciata) fails.

Dracaena trifasciata (syn. Sansevieria trifasciata) · Also called Sansevieria, Mother-in-law's tongue, Viper's bowstring hemp, لسان الحماة, نبتة الثعبان
By the PlantsWorld team · Updated 12 November 2026

Snake Plant quick facts

LightBright indirect is best; copes with low light. Gentle morning sun is fine, harsh summer sun is not.
Water, Mar–OctWhen the soil is dry to the bottom of the pot. Test it with a skewer first.
Water, Nov–FebLess often, as growth slows. NC State Extension: every one to two months in winter.
TemperatureGrows well at normal room temperature. Copes with summer heat in shade if the soil dries out. Protect from cold below about 10–13 °C.
HumidityTolerates low humidity. In humid coastal homes the soil dries more slowly, so water less often.
AC toleranceHigh, but keep it out of the direct stream of cold air from a vent.
Outdoors in UAEYes, in shade. Avoid midday sun May–Sep and cold inland nights.
PetsToxic to cats and dogs if chewed; keep away from young children.
Size indoorsAbout 15 cm ('Hahnii') to 120 cm (tall types).
GrowthSlow indoors, slower in low light.

Is a snake plant right for you?

A good fit if

  • You are new to plants, or you travel and sometimes forget to water.
  • Your room has medium or low light, such as a bedroom, a hallway or an office corner.
  • Your home or office runs AC for most of the year.
  • You want a plant that grows slowly and keeps its size for years.

Think twice if

  • A cat, a dog or a young child in your home chews plants: snake plants are toxic if eaten.
  • You like to water often, or your pots have no drainage hole.
  • You want fast growth or regular flowers.

How much light does a snake plant need?

A snake plant grows best in bright, indirect light, such as near an east-facing window (Clemson Extension: bright indirect light in the mornings). It also survives in low light (a dim hallway, an office corner, a bedroom with curtains), but it grows very slowly there and the leaf colour fades.

In the UAE, the main risk for a snake plant is too much sun, not too little. Afternoon sun through west- or south-facing glass in summer burns the leaves and causes pale or brown dry patches that never recover. Filter that sun with a sheer curtain, or move the plant back from the glass.

How often should you water a snake plant in Dubai?

Water a snake plant only when the soil is dry all the way to the bottom of the pot, not on a schedule. To test, push a wooden skewer to the bottom of the pot and pull it out. If the skewer comes out damp or with soil stuck to it, wait and test again later.

How fast snake plant soil dries depends on the pot, the room and the season. Small and terracotta pots in a warm, bright spot dry fastest; large plastic or glazed pots in a dim AC room stay damp longest. In humid coastal homes and after rain, snake plant soil dries slowly, so the test will tell you to water less often. Inland, dry heat and hot wind dry pots quickly, so test outdoor snake plants more often in summer.

In the cooler months snake plant growth slows and the soil takes longer to dry. NC State Extension says to water only every one to two months in winter, and University of Illinois Extension says to give just enough water in winter to stop the leaves from shrivelling.

When you water a snake plant, water thoroughly until water runs out of the drainage hole, then empty the saucer once the pot stops dripping. Never leave the pot standing in water.

UAE tap water is desalinated and then remineralised, and its mineral content varies by area and building. If you see a white crust on the soil or pot, or brown leaf tips, flush the pot with plenty of water to wash the salts out, or switch to filtered water.

  • Water the soil, not into the centre of the leaf rosette. Water sitting there can rot the base.
  • When in doubt, wait and test the soil again. A thirsty snake plant recovers; a waterlogged one often does not.

What soil and pot does a snake plant need?

Use a fast-draining mix for a snake plant: a cactus and succulent soil, or regular potting soil with plenty of perlite or coarse sand mixed in. Heavy, water-holding garden soil keeps the roots wet and leads to rot.

Always give a snake plant a pot with a drainage hole. Decorative pots without holes are fine as an outer cover, as long as you lift the inner pot out to drain. Terracotta and cement pots dry faster than plastic or glazed ceramic, which helps prevent overwatering.

Should you fertilise a snake plant?

Yes, but snake plants need very little feeding. Penn State Extension advises an all-purpose fertiliser at half strength once a month in the growing season: in the UAE, from March to October. Do not feed from November to February, when growth slows down. Too much fertiliser causes brown leaf tips and salt build-up on a snake plant, so less is better than more.

When and how should you repot a snake plant?

Repot a snake plant only when the roots fill the pot: roots come out of the drainage hole, the pot bulges or cracks, or water runs straight through. Penn State Extension says about every 5 years, and every 3 years for the compact 'Hahnii', because snake plants grow slowly and like a snug pot.

When you repot a snake plant, go up only one pot size: Colorado State University Extension advises a pot one to two inches (about 2.5–5 cm) wider. A pot that is much bigger than the roots holds wet soil the roots cannot use, and that leads to rot. In the UAE the best months are October–November and February–April. Avoid the summer peak, and let a new plant settle before you repot it.

  1. Choose a pot about 2.5–5 cm wider than the old one, with a drainage hole, and fresh fast-draining succulent mix.
  2. Ease the plant out of the old pot. Squeeze or tap a plastic pot to loosen the root ball.
  3. Shake off the loose old soil and cut away any black, soft roots with clean scissors.
  4. Set the plant at the same depth as before, fill around it with the new mix and press it down gently.
  5. Do not water straight away. Give any cut or broken roots time to dry and seal first; wait longer if you cut many roots or the room is cool.

How do you propagate a snake plant?

Division is the easiest and fastest way to propagate a snake plant, and it is the only way to keep a yellow leaf edge. Leaf cuttings also root, but slowly: University of Arkansas Extension says they take about three months to root and send up a new shoot, and cuttings from yellow-edged varieties grow back plain green.

To take snake plant leaf cuttings, cut a leaf into 5–8 cm sections. Make the lower cut slanted so you know which end goes down, and let the cut ends dry until they form a dry skin. Then stand them upright, bottom end down, in barely damp succulent soil, because they rot if kept too wet. They also root in water if you change the water often.

  1. Take the plant out of its pot and shake off the loose soil.
  2. Cut through the root mass with a clean knife so each piece has leaves and its own roots.
  3. Pot each piece in its own small pot of succulent mix.
  4. Let the cut surfaces dry before the first watering, then care for each piece as a normal snake plant.

Where should you place a snake plant at home or in the office?

Snake plants suit bedrooms, living-room corners, office desks and reception areas because they tolerate lower light and AC rooms year-round.

Do not put a snake plant directly under an AC vent, next to a sunny glass wall, or on a balcony in summer without shade. Tall snake plants make good floor plants beside a sofa or TV unit; compact types like 'Hahnii' and the starfish snake plant suit shelves and desks.

Move a snake plant between an AC room and the outdoors gradually: start with short spells in full shade and leave it outside for longer step by step. Watch the leaves: if pale or bleached patches appear, move it back into deeper shade and go more slowly. Go more slowly in the hottest months and with a plant that comes from a dim room. Never move it straight from AC into full summer heat or sun.

What should you do in the first week after your snake plant arrives?

A new snake plant needs time to settle in. The main risk in the first week is too much care, not too little.

  1. Put the plant in bright indirect light, away from direct sun and from AC vents.
  2. Leave it in one spot. Moving it again and again slows the settling in.
  3. Test the soil with a skewer before the first watering, and water only when it is dry to the bottom of the pot.
  4. Do not repot straight away. Let the plant settle in its delivery pot first, and repot only when the roots fill the pot.

How does snake plant care change through the UAE year?

Summer May–Sep

Indoors under AC a snake plant keeps growing slowly: water when the soil tests dry to the bottom of the pot. Keep it out of direct sun through glass. Outdoor plants need full shade; test the soil more often in heatwaves, because small and terracotta pots dry fastest.

Autumn Oct–Nov

Autumn is the best time to repot and divide a snake plant, and to move plants back to balconies and terraces (gradually, starting in shade). Feed once a month until the end of October. From November growth slows and the soil takes longer to dry.

Winter Dec–Feb

Snake plant growth slows down. Water less: the soil takes longer to dry, so test it before each watering (NC State Extension: every one to two months in winter). Stop feeding. Coastal winter nights are mild enough. Inland (Al Ain, desert areas) and in Riyadh or Kuwait, nights can fall below about 10–13 °C, the lowest a snake plant tolerates: move outdoor plants to a sheltered spot or indoors on cold nights. Make sure outdoor pots drain after rain.

Spring Mar–Apr

Start to feed a snake plant again once a month. Spring is a good second window for repotting. Move outdoor plants into shade before May.

Why are my snake plant leaves turning yellow and soft, and how do I save it from root rot?

Yellow, soft or mushy snake plant leaves almost always mean overwatering and root rot. The soil stays wet, and the roots suffocate and begin to rot from the base upward.

How to tell: Soil still damp days after watering, a soft or dark base, a sour smell from the pot.

How to fix it:

  1. Stop watering.
  2. Take the plant out of the pot and remove all soil.
  3. Cut off every black, mushy root and any rotten leaves with clean scissors.
  4. Leave the plant out of the pot, in the shade, until the cut root ends look dry.
  5. Repot in fresh, dry succulent soil in a pot with a drainage hole.
  6. Do not water straight away. Give the cut roots time to seal, then water only when the soil tests dry.

Helps: Succulent & Cactus Soil Mix

Why are my snake plant leaf tips turning brown?

Brown, dry tips on a snake plant usually come from salt and mineral build-up in the soil, from the minerals in tap water or from too much fertiliser. The salts stay behind in the pot as the water dries out.

How to tell: Crispy brown tips, sometimes with a white crust on the soil or pot rim.

How to fix it:

  1. Flush the soil with plenty of water and let it drain fully.
  2. Switch to filtered water if the crust keeps coming back.
  3. Cut fertiliser to half strength, March–October only.
  4. Trim the brown tips with clean scissors, following the natural leaf shape. Cut tips do not grow back.

Why are my snake plant leaves wrinkled or curling?

Wrinkled, thin or curling leaves mean the snake plant is not getting enough water. Either the soil has been bone dry for too long, or rotten roots can no longer take water up.

How to tell: Dry soil pulling away from the pot edge (thirst), or wet soil with a soft base (root damage).

How to fix it:

  1. If the soil is dry, water thoroughly. If the leaves do not firm up afterwards, check the roots.
  2. If the soil is wet, check the roots and follow the root rot fix for yellow, soft leaves.

Why is my snake plant falling over?

Snake plant leaves that bend, flop or fall outward are weak from overwatering or from too little light, which makes them grow tall and thin. A top-heavy plant in a light plastic pot can also tip over.

How to tell: Leaves bend at the base, look stretched, or the whole plant leans.

How to fix it:

  1. Check that the soil dries between waterings.
  2. Move the plant to brighter indirect light.
  3. Tie floppy leaves loosely together for support, or remove damaged leaves at the base.
  4. Repot into a heavier terracotta or cement pot if it keeps tipping.

What are the pale or brown dry patches on my snake plant?

Pale, bleached or brown papery patches on a snake plant are sunburn. This is common in the UAE when a plant sits in afternoon sun behind glass, or outdoors in summer without shade.

How to tell: Dry patches on the side facing the window or the sun, often soon after a move to a sunnier spot.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the plant out of direct sun or add a sheer curtain.
  2. The damaged patches will not heal. Leave them, or remove badly burnt leaves at the base.

What is the white cotton at the base of my snake plant leaves?

White, cottony clusters between snake plant leaves are mealybugs, a sap-sucking pest. They hide deep in the leaf base and spread to nearby plants.

How to tell: White fluff, sticky residue, slow growth, yellowing spots.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the plant away from other plants.
  2. Wipe off the bugs with a cotton bud dipped in rubbing alcohol.
  3. Spray the whole plant, especially the leaf bases, with a houseplant spray such as a neem-based product. Follow the label and repeat as it allows until no new mealybugs appear.

Helps: Neem Shield – Herbal Pesticide

Why are there tiny flies around my snake plant?

Small black flies around snake plant soil are fungus gnats. They breed in soil that stays wet, so they are a sign of overwatering.

How to tell: Tiny flies rising from the soil when you touch the pot.

How to fix it:

  1. Let the soil dry out completely before watering again.
  2. Yellow sticky traps catch the adults.

Why is my snake plant not growing?

Snake plants are naturally slow, and in low light or in winter they can stop growing for months. That is normal and not a sign of a problem as long as the leaves stay firm and green.

How to tell: No new leaves for several months, but healthy-looking existing leaves.

How to fix it:

  1. Move it to brighter indirect light.
  2. Feed once a month from March to October.
  3. Be patient. Growth starts again when the plant gets more light.

What mistakes kill a snake plant?

MistakeDo this instead
Watering on a fixed weekly scheduleWater only when the soil is dry all the way down. Test it with a skewer before each watering.
A pot with no drainage hole, or a saucer left full of waterUse a pot with a hole, or lift the inner pot out of a cover pot to drain. Empty the saucer once the pot stops dripping.
Pouring water into the centre of the leavesWater the soil around the plant. Water that sits in the leaf centre can rot the base.
Summer afternoon sun behind a west- or south-facing windowBright indirect light, or a sheer curtain on the window.
A spot right under an AC ventKeep the plant out of the direct stream of cold air. With the AC on, hold your hand next to the leaves: if you feel the air moving, move the plant further away or turn the louvres away from it.
Repotting into a much bigger potGo up one pot size only. Colorado State University Extension advises a pot about 2.5–5 cm wider.
Feeding in winter or at full strengthHalf-strength all-purpose fertiliser once a month, March to October only.

Snake Plant myths and facts

MythFact
A snake plant needs water every week.A snake plant needs water only when the soil is dry to the bottom of the pot. Under AC the soil dries slowly, so test it with a skewer instead of following a calendar.
Misting helps a snake plant under AC.Snake plants do not need misting, and water that collects in the leaf centre can rot the base. Wipe the dust off the leaves instead.
A bigger pot makes a snake plant grow faster.A pot much bigger than the roots stays wet and causes root rot. Snake plants grow best in a snug pot.
A leaf cutting from a yellow-edged snake plant keeps its yellow edge.Leaf cuttings from yellow-edged varieties usually grow back plain green. Only division keeps the yellow edge.

Is a snake plant safe for cats and dogs?

No. The ASPCA lists the snake plant as toxic to cats and dogs. The leaves contain saponins, which can cause nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea if a pet chews them. Keep the plant out of reach of pets and young children.

If your pet chewed it: Call your vet or a 24-hour animal emergency clinic straight away and tell them the plant name. Do not wait for symptoms.

Snake Plant FAQs

Can a snake plant live in a room with no window?

A snake plant can live in a room with no window only under good electric light, because it needs some light to make its food. Under bright LED or office lighting that is on for long hours, a snake plant survives but grows very slowly. In a room that stays dark it uses up its stored reserves and dies, so move it to a window if it stops growing, fades or leans.

Does a snake plant clean the air?

A snake plant does not noticeably clean the air in a normal room. Studies that found snake plants removing chemicals were done in small sealed chambers, and a home would need far more plants than anyone keeps to match fresh air from ventilation. Buy it because it looks good and is easy to keep, not as an air filter.

Can a snake plant live outside in the UAE?

Yes, a snake plant can live outside in the UAE in shade, and it grows well outdoors from October to April. From May to September keep it in full shade, out of the midday and afternoon sun, and test the soil more often in heatwaves, because pots dry out fast. Move it outside gradually, not straight from an AC room. In winter it is happy on the coast, but inland and in colder GCC cities protect it from nights below about 10–13 °C.

Is a snake plant good for the bedroom?

Yes, a snake plant is a practical bedroom plant. It copes with low light and AC rooms, needs little care, and unlike most plants it takes in carbon dioxide at night. One snake plant will not noticeably change the air in a room.

Can a snake plant grow in water?

A snake plant can be kept in water with only the roots submerged, and leaf cuttings root in water. Change the water often to keep it clean (UConn Extension advises daily for rooting cuttings) and keep the leaves dry. In water it grows more slowly and less reliably than in free-draining soil, so pot it up if it starts to struggle.

Does a snake plant flower?

A snake plant flowers only occasionally, and snake plants kept indoors rarely flower. Older plants sometimes send up a stalk of small, fragrant, greenish-white to cream flowers.

How long does a snake plant live?

With basic care a snake plant lives for many years, and it keeps producing new shoots that you can divide into new plants.

Why is a snake plant a popular gift in the UAE?

A snake plant forgives missed waterings and looks good in modern homes and offices. That makes it a common housewarming, Eid and corporate gift.

Ordering from PlantsWorld

How is plant size measured?

Size is measured from the bottom of the nursery pot to the top tip of the highest leaf. A plant listed as 50-60 CM stands in that range measured this way.

Which pot option should I choose, nursery or decorative?

Choose the nursery pot for the lowest price or if you already have a planter. Choose a decorative pot for a ready-to-display plant that arrives fully potted with soil mix, perlite and a drainage layer. The plant itself is the same.

Do the decorative pots have drainage holes?

Decorative pot orders include a drainage layer at the base, with premium soil mix and perlite. For specific details on a particular pot model, send us the product link and our team will confirm.

Is the plant healthy on arrival? Can I check first?

Plants are guaranteed to arrive healthy. Check your plant with the delivery agent: if it's damaged or not what you ordered, you can refuse it on the spot. If you find damage after unpacking, send photos and your order number on WhatsApp (+971 4 294 1422) or email sales@plantsworld.ae within 24 hours and we'll replace it free. You can also ask for a pre-dispatch photo.

Will my plant be safe in the UAE heat during delivery?

Yes. Our own delivery team brings your order, not a third-party courier. In extreme summer heat (June to September) we may move deliveries to farther emirates to a cooler day and agree the new day with you. If anything arrives damaged, we replace it free.

Will my plant look exactly like the website photo?

You'll receive the variety and size you ordered, but every plant grows individually, so leaf count, shape and shade can differ from the photo, which is representative. For peace of mind, ask for a pre-dispatch photo at checkout or on WhatsApp.

Something looks wrong with your plant?

Send us photos on WhatsApp and our team will tell you what is happening and what to do. These five photos help us answer fast:

  1. The whole plant, from a step back
  2. A close-up of the problem leaf, front and back
  3. The soil surface and the pot, with the drainage hole if there is one
  4. Where the plant stands: the window, the AC vent and the light
